stem: During NHSN surgical-site-infection surveillance, an infection initially met superficial-incisional SSI criteria. Later, within the designated surveillance period, the same event meets deep-incisional SSI criteria. How should the infection-prevention nurse report the event?

options.A: Keep the original superficial-incisional classification because the first classification can never be changed
options.B: Edit the event to reflect the deepest tissue level that meets SSI criteria—deep incisional in this case—and update the event date according to NHSN instructions
options.C: Automatically classify the event as organ/space because any progression beyond superficial tissue is organ/space infection
options.D: Remove the event from NHSN surveillance because an SSI that changes tissue level is no longer reportable

rationale: NHSN requires the entire SSI protocol to be followed. If a superficial-incisional SSI progresses and meets criteria at a deeper tissue level during the designated surveillance period, the event type and date are edited to reflect the deepest tissue level where SSI criteria are met. Deep-incisional and organ/space definitions are distinct; progression does not automatically make an event organ/space.
educational_objective: Apply current NHSN surveillance rules when a surgical-site infection progresses to a deeper tissue level during the surveillance period.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — NHSN
source_document_title: FAQs: Surgical Site Infections (SSI) Events; Chapter 9 Surgical Site Infection Event
source_locator: SSI FAQ Q25–Q26; Chapter 9 January 2026: when superficial SSI progresses deeper within surveillance period, edit event type/date to deepest tissue level meeting criteria
source_claim_supported: NHSN SSI classification is a surveillance/reporting framework and requires updating the event to the deepest tissue level meeting criteria during the surveillance period.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection surveillance and prevention
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — SSI surveillance
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported source claim that NHSN SSI classification guides treatment. Rebuilt the item around the explicit 2026 surveillance rule requiring classification at the deepest tissue level met during the surveillance period.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: CDC NHSN January 2026 SSI protocol and FAQ verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Deepest-tissue reporting rule, event editing and distinction between deep-incisional and organ/space are source-supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; NHSN explicitly requires editing when deeper criteria are met.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; organ/space requires its own criteria and site-specific definition.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; progression does not invalidate reporting.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B follows the 2026 NHSN reporting instruction.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked treatment-versus-surveillance scope, surveillance-period timing, deep-incisional versus organ/space criteria and event-date update; no unresolved conflict.
